non_utc_verification.why: Phase 8 computes drift on scan finalisation, so a lifecycle that cannot publish on a non-UTC database server means the phase's own feature never fires.
non_utc_verification.method: the disposable cluster's postgresql.conf timezone was set to Australia/Melbourne and reloaded; both suites re-run in full

after_phase8.note: Correcting the eleven comparison sites was NOT sufficient on its own: the two naive columns those comparisons read (scan_dispatch.available_at, scan.last_progress_at) still defaulted to a bare now(), which PostgreSQL converts using the server TimeZone, so a new dispatch row was stamped ahead of the UTC clock it is compared against. Both defaults were corrected too.

remediation.why: A six-dimension adversarial review of the code that actually landed, with independent refuters per finding, produced 34 findings against a fully green suite. The suite passing was never the question; what it did not catch was.
fixed: CRITICAL verify_remediation accepted a run that never compared the finding's axis or its control as proof of remediation. Now requires the axis comparable AND the control absent from controls_skipped. Two regression tests, both confirmed failing without the fix.

CRITICAL POST /v1/drift/runs enqueued worker.tasks.evaluate_drift, which no worker registered; the endpoint answered 202 and the task was discarded. Task registered; a contract test now reads the literal name from the backend source and asserts the worker registers it.

HIGH Neither create_connection nor update_connection persisted the Purview binding, so the whole Wave A chain was unreachable from the API. 28 tests now cover create, update, half-binding rejection and clearing as a pair.
HIGH engine/worker/tasks.py never passed the Purview binding to PowerShellClient; a promoted compliance control would have failed request validation before reaching the tenant.
HIGH Drift never fired on the retry-exhausted finalisation path, so whether a scan was compared depended on which control finished last. The test that encoded this bug was corrected and split.

HIGH Rotating DRIFT_FACT_HMAC_KEY manufactured a configuration-changed event for every declared fact against an untouched tenant. A rotation is now an honest comparability break (fingerprint_key_rotated).
HIGH member_digests and member_tokens were sorted independently and so were not parallel arrays; set-member events could name the wrong value.
HIGH CIS 3.2.2 used an existential quantifier where the audit applies steps 4 and 5 to every returned policy, and returned a determinate FALSE for E3 tenants outside its E5-only profile.

MEDIUM promote_candidate.py was single-use and could never succeed on the shipped metadata formatting. The edit is now surgical (four lines changed, all other bytes preserved) and the full three-candidate sequence was exercised end to end.
Found while fixing the above: drift_baseline.key_id existed in neither the migration nor the ORM model, so the column did not exist in the database and the rotation guard would have been dead code.
recorded_not_fixed: drift_notification.thread_key is the unkeyed event_key and baseline_id is on the same row, so a holder of only that table can brute-force which control and fact a thread concerns. Fix specified in the handoff; not attempted because it threads through ~10 call sites and a half-applied change would be worse.
SKIP_PROJECTION_CHANGED can never fire: projection_id derives only from collector_id with no version bump, so a changed FieldSpec would compare incompatible shapes instead of skipping.
